title: Pikachu Went to Space, and Now It Is Helping Celebrate World Space Week
summary:
Pikachu has officially been to space! The European Space Agency, or ESA, revealed on September 19, 2026, that a special Pikachu plush toy spent 67 days on the International Space Station, or ISS. Now that space trip is part of World Space Week, which runs from October 4 through 10 this year.

The plush "astronaut" blasted off to the ISS on April 11 aboard a Cygnus cargo spacecraft. It came back to Earth on June 17 on a SpaceX Dragon cargo spacecraft. While it was in orbit, Pikachu traveled around Earth about 1,040 times.

ESA timed the mission to kick off World Space Week 2026. To celebrate, the agency created a special exhibit that mixes real space science with Pokémon characters. Visitors can see displays about Europe's space missions and what life is like on the ISS. They can also learn how ESA studies the Sun, the solar system and the rest of the universe.

The exhibit opened at ESA's headquarters in Paris, France, in late September. It will travel to museums and other places across Europe until April 2027.

Pokémon GO players can join in, too. From October 4, 2026, through April 30, 2027, players who visit participating science and space museums in Europe can take part in special activities. These include One-Star Raids featuring Astronaut Pikachu, research tasks and chances to find event-themed Pokémon.

ESA hopes the project will make kids and teens curious about space and science. "Inspiring future generations is a key part of ESA's mission," said Josef Aschbacher, the head of ESA.
why_it_matters: Space agencies use popular characters like Pikachu to spark young people's interest in science, which could inspire the next generation of scientists and astronauts.
